answer: Running 279 aliases therefore means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest participants do not face at scale. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the saffron schedule in the sable ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the river checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 5 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. That is 39 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
